title: Element distinctness and k-distinctness
problem_latex:

quantum_latex:
\textbf{Element distinctness.} $\Theta(n^{2/3})$ queries by the Ambainis Johnson-graph quantum walk, with $\widetilde O(n^{2/3})$ time when the walk data structure supports coherent updates.

\textbf{$k$-distinctness.} $O(n^{1-2^{k-2}/(2^k-1)})$ queries by Belovs' learning graph; the bound is for constant $k$.
classical_latex:
\textbf{Element distinctness.} $\Theta(n)$ randomized queries; hashing gives expected $O(n)$ word-RAM time and sorting gives $O(n\log n)$ comparison time.

\textbf{$k$-distinctness.} $\Theta(n)$ queries, with expected $O(n)$ word-RAM time by counting equal keys.

title: Polynomial interpolation over finite fields
problem_latex:
\textbf{Univariate polynomial interpolation over finite fields.} Given evaluation-oracle access to an unknown polynomial $f\in\mathbb F_q[x]$ with $\deg f\le d<q$, output its coefficients. Complexity counts oracle evaluations; success probabilities depend on the field-size regime.

\textbf{Multivariate polynomial interpolation over finite fields.} $M$ evaluations suffice by multivariate interpolation and are information-theoretically necessary for exact reconstruction. The query ratio is approximately $(n+d)/d$.

title: Jones polynomial approximation
problem_latex:
\textbf{Jones polynomial of a plat closure.} Given an $n$-strand braid $b$ of length $m$, a permitted root of unity $t=e^{2\pi i/k}$ and $\varepsilon>0$, estimate the Jones polynomial of its plat closure to the additive scale $\varepsilon d^{n/2-1}$, where $d=2\cos(\pi/k)$. Complexity is in the finite braid description.

\textbf{Jones polynomial of a trace closure.} Given a braid and a permitted fixed root of unity, estimate the Jones polynomial of its trace closure to inverse-polynomial additive error after the Markov-trace normalization. Input and output are finite braid data and a numerical estimate.
quantum_latex:
\textbf{Jones polynomial of a plat closure.} $\operatorname{poly}(n,m,k,1/\varepsilon)$ quantum time by Aharonov--Jones--Landau, using the path-model braid representation and a Hadamard test.

\textbf{Jones polynomial of a trace closure.} $\operatorname{poly}(n,m,1/\varepsilon)$ time in the one-clean-qubit model by Shor--Jordan, using normalized-trace estimation of the path-model braid representation.
classical_latex:
\textbf{Jones polynomial of a plat closure.} Classical tensor contraction or state-vector evaluation takes $\exp(O(n))\operatorname{poly}(m,k,1/\varepsilon)$ time, with width-dependent improvements. At universal fixed roots and inverse-polynomial normalized error, efficient classical approximation would imply $\mathsf{BQP}=\mathsf{BPP}$. For an implemented $q$-qubit, $g$-gate circuit over a fixed finite algebraic gate set, classical simulation also gives $\min\{O(g2^q),\operatorname{poly}(g)2^{O(w)},\operatorname{poly}(s)2^{O(s/\sqrt{\log s})}\}$. Here $w$ is a contraction width and $s$ is the size of the sparse bounded-fan-in Boolean encoding of scalar path counts at the required precision; gate synthesis and precision contribute to $g,s$.

\textbf{Jones polynomial of a trace closure.} General exact contraction is exponential in braid width. A polynomial-time classical algorithm for the complete normalized approximation regime would place $\mathsf{DQC1}$ inside $\mathsf{BPP}$. For an implemented $q$-qubit, $g$-gate circuit over a fixed finite algebraic gate set, classical simulation also gives $\min\{O(g2^q),\operatorname{poly}(g)2^{O(w)},\operatorname{poly}(s)2^{O(s/\sqrt{\log s})}\}$. Here $w$ is a contraction width and $s$ is the size of the sparse bounded-fan-in Boolean encoding of scalar path counts at the required precision; gate synthesis and precision contribute to $g,s$.

title: Junta testing
problem_latex:
\textbf{Junta testing with membership queries.} Given $f:\{0,1\}^n\to\{0,1\}$ by a coherent membership oracle, distinguish functions depending on at most $k$ variables from functions at uniform Hamming distance at least $\varepsilon$ from every such function.

\textbf{Junta testing from quantum examples.} Distinguish $k$-juntas from functions $\varepsilon$-far from every $k$-junta using copies of $2^{-n/2}\sum_x|x,f(x)\rangle$. Classical access consists of independent uniform labeled examples.

\textbf{Distribution-free junta testing.} Given membership queries to $f:\{0,1\}^n\to\{0,1\}$ and sampling access to an unknown distribution $D$, distinguish $k$-juntas from functions with $\Pr_D[f(x)\ne g(x)]\ge\varepsilon$ for every $k$-junta $g$. The quantum model coherently accesses the specified oracles.
quantum_latex:
\textbf{Junta testing with membership queries.} $\Theta(\min\{2^{n/2},\sqrt{\log(2+\varepsilon 2^k)/\varepsilon}\})$ queries for $n\ge2k$ and $0<\varepsilon\le1/8$, by the optimal Boolean-junta tester. In the range $\varepsilon\ge2^{-k/16}$ this simplifies to $\Theta(\sqrt{k/\varepsilon})$.

\textbf{Junta testing from quantum examples.} $O(k/\varepsilon)$ quantum examples by Atici--Servedio Fourier sampling, testing whether observed Fourier supports fit within $k$ coordinates.

\textbf{Distribution-free junta testing.} $O(k/\varepsilon)$ queries by Belovs' distribution-free quantum junta tester.
classical_latex:
\textbf{Junta testing with membership queries.} $O(\min\{2^n,k\log k+k/\varepsilon\})$ classical queries by junta testing or truth-table acquisition, with $\Omega(k\log k)$ required at constant distance.

\textbf{Junta testing from quantum examples.} Passive classical examples require a number growing with $n$, even for small fixed $k$; exhaustive empirical testing of all $k$-coordinate functions uses $O((k\log n+2^k)/\varepsilon^2)$ samples.

\textbf{Distribution-free junta testing.} $O((k/\varepsilon)\log(k/\varepsilon))$ adaptive queries by classical distribution-free junta testing, with an $\Omega(k\log k)$ lower bound at constant distance.

title: Learning DNF from quantum examples
problem_latex:
\textbf{Learning DNF under the uniform distribution.} An unknown $s$-term DNF $f:\{0,1\}^n\to\{0,1\}$ supplies uniform quantum examples. Output a classical hypothesis $h$ with $\Pr[h(x)\ne f(x)]\le\varepsilon$ and confidence $1-\delta$. Complexity counts examples and computation.

\textbf{Learning DNF under product distributions.} Given quantum examples of an unknown $s$-term DNF under a product distribution with $\mu_i=\mathbb E[x_i]\in[-1+c,1-c]$ for constant $c>0$, output a hypothesis of error at most $\varepsilon$. The marginal biases are known or learned as in the algorithm.
quantum_latex:
\textbf{Learning DNF under the uniform distribution.} $\operatorname{poly}(n,s,1/\varepsilon,\log(1/\delta))$ time and quantum examples by Bshouty--Jackson, combining Fourier sampling and boosting.

\textbf{Learning DNF under product distributions.} $\operatorname{poly}(n,s,1/\varepsilon,\log(1/\delta))$ time for constant $c$, by Kanade--Rocchetto--Severini biased Fourier sampling and the product-distribution DNF learner.
classical_latex:
\textbf{Learning DNF under the uniform distribution.} $n^{O(\log(s/\varepsilon))}\operatorname{poly}(\log(1/\delta))$ time by classical low-degree approximation and uniform-distribution DNF learning. Classical membership-query learning is polynomial in the stronger active-query model.

\textbf{Learning DNF under product distributions.} $n^{O_c(\log(s/\varepsilon))}$ time by low-degree biased-Fourier approximation and classical regression; the general distribution-independent DNF learner has $2^{\widetilde O(n^{1/3})}$ time for polynomial-size DNF.

title: Learning symmetric juntas
problem_latex:
\textbf{Learning an exact-half junta.} An unknown $S\subseteq[n]$ has known even size $k$. Query access is to $f_S(x)=[\sum_{i\in S}x_i=k/2]$. Recover $S$ with bounded error; each query can specify a superposition of $n$-bit inputs.

\textbf{Learning a majority junta.} An unknown $S\subseteq[n]$ of known size $k$ defines $f_S(x)=[\sum_{i\in S}x_i\ge k/2]$, with the paper's tie convention. Given membership queries, recover $S$.
quantum_latex:
\textbf{Learning an exact-half junta.} $\Theta(k^{1/4})$ queries by Belovs' adversary-bound algorithm, with efficient implementations described in the subsequent symmetric-junta learning work.

\textbf{Learning a majority junta.} $O(k^{1/4})$ queries by Belovs' symmetric-junta adversary algorithm; time-efficient variants incur additional logarithmic and input-description factors.
classical_latex:
\textbf{Learning an exact-half junta.} $\Omega(k\log(n/k))$ classical binary queries by information theory for $k\le n/2$; finite-class elimination provides a general upper bound and active learning exploits the symmetric predicate.

\textbf{Learning a majority junta.} $\Omega(k\log(n/k))$ classical binary queries for $k\le n/2$, by distinguishing the $\binom nk$ candidate supports.

title: Identity and uniformity testing of finite distributions
problem_latex:
\textbf{Uniformity testing of a finite distribution.} Given coherent access to a classical sampler for $p$ on $[N]$, distinguish $p=u_N$ from $\|p-u_N\|_1\ge\varepsilon$, where $u_N(i)=1/N$. Classical access uses ordinary independent samples.

\textbf{Identity testing of a finite distribution.} Given a known distribution $q$ on $[N]$ and coherent sampler access to $p$, distinguish $p=q$ from $\|p-q\|_1\ge\varepsilon$. The known probabilities of $q$ can be evaluated as required by the reduction.
quantum_latex:
\textbf{Uniformity testing of a finite distribution.} $O(N^{1/3}/\varepsilon^2)$ coherent sampler queries by Bravyi--Harrow--Hassidim and Chakraborty--Fischer--Matsliah--de Wolf; the $N^{1/3}$ dependence is optimal at constant distance.

\textbf{Identity testing of a finite distribution.} $O(N^{1/3}\log^2N\log\log N/\varepsilon^5)$ queries by Chakraborty--Fischer--Matsliah--de Wolf via reduction to uniformity testing.
classical_latex:
\textbf{Uniformity testing of a finite distribution.} $\Theta(\sqrt N/\varepsilon^2)$ samples by collision or chi-square uniformity testers in the standard nondegenerate range.

\textbf{Identity testing of a finite distribution.} $\Theta(\sqrt N/\varepsilon^2)$ samples in the worst case over known reference distributions, with sharper instance-dependent bounds for a specified $q$.

title: PAC learning in the large-error regime
problem_latex: For a constructive $\lambda(n)$ satisfying $n^{\omega(1)}2^{-n/2}\le\lambda(n)\le n^{-\omega(1)}$, learn the concept class constructed by Oliveira from uniform quantum examples: output a classical circuit agreeing with the target on at least $1/2+\lambda(n)$ of inputs with probability at least $1-n^{-k}$, for fixed $k$.
quantum_latex: $\operatorname{poly}(n)$ time and examples by correlation-biased sampling of quadratic hypotheses and boosting. The general learner using $m$ examples achieves advantage $\Omega(\sqrt{m/2^n})$, failure $O(1/m)$ and time $m\operatorname{poly}(n)$.
classical_latex: For the constructed class, no polynomial-time randomized membership-query learner attains even agreement $1/2+\lambda(n)/n^k$ with success above $n^{-k}$ on every target. Querying the complete effective truth table uses $O(n^{3k}\lambda(n)^{-2})$ queries up to polynomial factors from the construction.
